<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

**Splits each paged attention translation unit on one more item: `block_size`.** `main` (#62475) splits the kernels per (query dtype, kv-cache dtype, head size), giving 12 units, and each of those units still instantiates *both* block sizes and picks one at runtime. **Thus, we now have 24 kernels instead of 12.**

We introduce a generator for these 24 units instead of hand-writting each file: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/generate_paged_attn.py

This PR is part of a 5-PRs series with #62717 (topk softplus-sqrt), #62718 (skinny GEMMs), #63364 (int4 skinny GEMM) and #63365 (fused MUSE-Spark op). All PRs are required for build time gain, see details below.

The single-arch rows are `pip install -e .` on MI350 (gfx950); the 9-arch row is the `setup.py bdist_wheel` described under *Validation*. All cold builds:

| build | `main` | this PR | All 5 PRs (#62921) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAX_JOBS=16`, gfx950 only | 107 s | 92 s | 87 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, gfx950 only | 85 s | 86 s | 50 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, 9 archs | 1263 s | 1261 s | 472 s |

## Claims

- Splits each unit on one more item, `block_size`: the runtime `switch (block_size)` inside `paged_attention_*` becomes an entry point per block size (introduced as a kernel dimension by #8310, kept as a runtime branch by #62475), so 12 units become 24 and each instantiates half the kernels.
- 14 % off the single-arch build at `MAX_JOBS=16`; neutral at `MAX_JOBS=64`, where another unit is the tail.
- ~190 lines of hand-written duplication removed: 12 units, 12 prototypes and a 50-line configure-time regex guard collapse into one variant list, so an instantiation can no longer exist without a dispatch arm - which is what the guard used to check.
- Navi-less builds instantiate 11 % fewer device kernels per unit; Navi (gfx11/gfx12) builds are unaffected.
- Nothing about what runs changes: same kernels, same dispatch order, same numerics.

### Why five PRs

The two builds are bound by different things, so no single change moves both.

**Why the three single-arch PRs are all needed.** At 1 arch (`gfx950`, `MAX_JOBS=64`, `main` = 85 s) three groups take turns setting the wall, in this order:

1. topk softplus-sqrt (#62717) - 74.5 s, a single unit
2. paged attention (#62716) - 71.6 s, the slowest of 12 units
3. other skinny GEMMs (#62718) - 40.9 s, a single unit

#62717 takes (1) to 7.4 s, #62716 takes (2) to 31.1 s and #62718 stops (3) from becoming the next tail; with all three the tail moves to `selective_scan_fwd` (37.7 s) and the build goes from 85 s to 49 s. Drop any one of them and a ~70 s unit is back at the top, so the single-arch win needs all three.

**Why that is not enough at 9 archs.** A 9-arch build multiplies every unit's time by ~9, and the tail becomes two files that none of the first three touch: `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` at 1232 s and `csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` at 478 s. All three merged take the 9-arch build from 1263 s to only 1253 s. #63364 splits the first (its tail drops to 448 s) and #63365 the second (to 171 s), which is what reaches 472 s.

The `skinny_gemms_int4.cu` tail is invisible in a `gfx950` build because that file **only emits its kernels for RDNA (that is part of the 9-arch build)**:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L17-L19
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L568-L579

`csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` fails differently: it has no arch guard, so a `gfx950` build compiles it for real - it is just 25 s there against 478 s across nine archs, which is why a single-arch profile ranks it as irrelevant (#63365).

| slowest unit per group, 1 arch (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| topk softplus-sqrt | 74.5 s | 7.4 s |
| paged attention | 71.6 s | 31.1 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | 40.9 s | 31.6 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 36.5 s | 37.7 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 25.0 s | 10.9 s |
| int4 skinny GEMM | 19.4 s | 17.5 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **76 s / 15.8x** | **39 s / 30.2x** |

| slowest unit per group, 9 archs (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| int4 skinny GEMM | 1232 s | 448 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 478 s | 171 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 288 s | 296 s |
| paged attention | 284 s | 286 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | not recorded | 247 s |
| topk softplus-sqrt | not recorded | 99 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **1234 s / 8.7x** | **472 s / 25x** |

## Validation

### Single arch build

```bash
PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx950" VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=N \
  pip install --no-cache-dir -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation
```

MI350 (gfx950), four builds run one after the other in the same container, each from a cleared tree (`vllm/*.so` and `build/` removed first), so every number is a cold build with no ccache and no shared CMake cache. Run-to-run variance is a few seconds, so the single-PR rows are indicative:

| | MAX_JOBS=16 | MAX_JOBS=64 |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (`main`, `f4edf9f0f0`) | 107 s | 85 s |
| **this PR** (`089bbaf68a`) | **92 s (−14 %)** | **86 s (≈0 %)** |
| #62717 topk softplus-sqrt 114a66d0f5 | 107 s (≈0 %) | 85 s (≈0 %) |
| #62718 skinny GEMMs 78a62ceb1c | 110 s (+3 %) | 85 s (≈0 %) |
| #63364 int4 skinny GEMM 6271426e4f | 109 s (+2 %) | 87 s (+2 %) |
| #63365 fused MUSE-Spark 31de254fe4 | 108 s (+1 %) | 87 s (+2 %) |
| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | 87 s (−19 %) | 50 s (−41 %) |

Environment, one host: AMD EPYC 9575F (64 cores / 256 threads), 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (251 GiB each), ROCm 10.0, `torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx950`, `PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_ENABLED=0`.

| check | configuration | result |
|---|---|---|
| `paged_attention` vs a torch reference over the paged KV cache (GQA aware) | fp16, bf16 x head 64/128 x block size 16/32 x gqa 1/4/6 | max abs err 3e-4 (fp16), 5e-3 (bf16) |
| fresh configure with no generated files present | generator runs at configure time | configure + build + link OK |
| moved kernel/launcher code vs the parent commit | scripted `git diff` of the moved ranges | empty modulo the intended edits |

Repo tests for the kernels this PR touches:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py
```

`393 passed, 14 warnings in 1732.99s (0:28:52)`

### 9 archs build

The multi-arch wheel build with the 9 release archs of `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`, mold as the linker and sccache disabled, from a cleared tree (`vllm/*.so`, `build/` and `dist/` removed first):

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold" \
  PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151" \
  VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=64 \
  python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist
```

The 9 release archs, one build at a time, same container and same command:

| build | wall time | wheel |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (`f4edf9f0f0`) | 1263 s | 266 MB |
| **this PR** (`089bbaf68a`) | **1261 s** | **275 MB** |
| #62717 topk softplus-sqrt 114a66d0f5 | 1243 s | 269 MB |
| #62718 skinny GEMMs 78a62ceb1c | 1248 s | 266 MB |
| #63364 int4 skinny GEMM 6271426e4f | **600 s (−52 %)** | **257 MB** |
| #63365 fused MUSE-Spark 31de254fe4 | **1241 s (−2 %)** | **266 MB** |
| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | **472 s (−63 %)** | **270 MB** |

At 9 archs the build is translation-unit-latency bound, not link bound: every host link is sub-second, so the wall is one long unit at a time. The split does not move that wall by itself - what it changes is that the link keeps succeeding. Pre-reland `main` (`db3b0f0fae`, i.e. #62475 without `--offload-compress`) fails this exact build with `mold: error: ... relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against .eh_frame out of range`, the failure #62983 reverted for.

## Details

Device code generation for one instantiation set is ~95 s of AMDGPU backend time, so a single file holding every (dtype, kv-cache dtype, head size) combination made the wall clock of the whole build that file. #62475 split it by hand, which left three things to keep in sync: the files, the prototypes in `attention_dispatch.cu` and the dispatch arms (hence the `file(READ)` + regex guard). Generating all three from one `VARIANTS` list removes that coupling:

- one translation unit per (variant, block size) - `block_size` moves from a runtime switch inside the entry point into the entry point name, which is what lets a unit instantiate a single block size;
- `attention_paged_attn_entries.inc`, the `ATTN_ENTRY()` prototypes, included at file scope;
- `attention_paged_attn_dispatch.inc`, the kv-cache-dtype / query-dtype / mfma-type / block-size / head-size dispatch of `paged_attention()`, included in its body.

The generated units do not depend on the arch list: whether the Navi (gfx11/gfx12) kernel set is instantiated is a `VLLM_ROCM_ATTN_NO_NAVI` compile definition that CMake derives from `VLLM_GPU_ARCHES` and sets on the `_rocm_C` target, so every build directory and arch list uses the same files (two builds can no longer overwrite each other's units). What is on disk is recorded in a stamp next to the outputs (`csrc/rocm/.paged_attn_generated`: the script hash plus the exact list of files written, gitignored) rather than in the CMake cache, and CMake takes the source list from that list instead of a glob: a stray or scratch `attention_paged_attn_*.cu` in `csrc/rocm/` is no longer compiled into `_rocm_C`, and a partially deleted set (any `.cu` **or** `.inc`, not just "all of them") triggers regeneration. The script is also in `CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS`, so editing it re-runs configure instead of leaving stale units behind. Separately, `-ftime-trace` attributed 6.9 s of the 11.5 s host frontend of a unit to `<torch/all.h>`, which pulls autograd, nn and jit into code that only needs `at::Tensor`, the CUDA stream/guard helpers and `TORCH_CHECK`; the header now includes the ATen/c10 surface only, which cuts both the host and the device parse by ~2/3.

**Change in behaviour.** Only one, and it is narrow: a build whose arch list has no `gfx11`/`gfx12` code objects now raises `TORCH_CHECK(!is_navi, ...)` instead of running a Navi launcher that no code object backs. The `mfma_type` handling keeps the previous semantics (the last arm is a plain `else`, so an unrecognised value still selects the f16 MFMA kernels rather than failing). Numerics are unchanged.

**How the matrix got this big.** The instantiation space this PR splits was grown one axis at a time:

| PR | landed | what it added to the instantiation space |
|---|---|---|
| #8310 | 2024-09-13 | initial ROCm paged attention: 4 kernels over `{fp16, bf16}` x head `{64, 128}` x block `{16, 32}` x alibi `{on, off}` |
| #8577 | 2024-09-19 | fp8 KV cache: the `KV_DTYPE` / `cache_t` axis |
| #12348 | 2025-03-04 | partition/reduce rewrite: 4 -> 6 kernels (`mfma16`, `mfma4`, `reduce`) |
| #17139 | 2025-05-07 | fp8 output fusion: `OUTT` becomes `uint8_t` when `fp8_out_scale` is set = x2 |
| #17004 | 2025-05-21 | RDNA/Navi: the whole set duplicated for gfx11/gfx12, 6 -> 12 `__global__` |
| #22222 | 2025-09-15 | fp8 attention update: adds `MFMAType` (`Fp8` vs `F16`) = x2 on the fp8 path |
| #42755 | 2026-10-15 | `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` added to all 12 kernels = +50 % |

So the matrix this PR splits is a product of six axes. This PR adds none of them; it cuts the product into 24 units.

### Left to do

Follow-ups identified while doing this, deliberately out of scope:

- [ ] Split the units further along `alibi` / `fp8_out_scale`: measured a loss while each unit paid ~20 s just to parse `attention_kernels.cuh`, which is ~6 s now.
- [ ] Cheaper debug info for HIP kernels: dropping `-g` saves ~18 % of a unit's compile time at 1 arch and more at 9 (`RelWithDebInfo` applies `-g` to every unit).
- [ ] `csrc/mamba/selective_scan_fwd` is the next tail once the two per-unit splits are in (296 s at 9 archs, 37.7 s at 1): split or prune its instantiations.
- [ ] `<torch/all.h>` still comes in transitively via `rocm/dispatch_utils.h`, which ~50 TUs include; trimming it there needs a CUDA build check.
- [ ] `hipify_all` is a single serial command (1.9 s) that every compile waits on - worth parallelising once the wall clock is ~10 s.
- [ ] Not done here on purpose: folding the 12 `VARIANTS` dicts into a product of three tables and dropping the redundant `clang-format off/on` pair around the generated include - refactor churn that does not change the build outcome.
- [ ] Not done here on purpose: `MANIFEST.in` has `recursive-include csrc *`, so an sdist built from an already-configured tree would ship the generated units (harmless, they are regenerated; CI sdists come from a clean clone), and the ROCm build docs do not yet mention that changing `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` regenerates these units.

+    """File and entry-point suffix, derived so it cannot disagree with the fields."""

+KV_CACHE_DTYPE_PREDICATES = {
+    "auto": 'kv_cache_dtype == "auto"',
+    "fp8": 'kv_cache_dtype == "fp8" || kv_cache_dtype == "fp8_e4m3"',

+

+

+# on disk were produced by the current version (same MD5 as `file(MD5 ...)`).
+# CMake passes the key it compares against so the format is defined in one place;
+# a manual run falls back to the hash above.
+with open(__file__, "rb") as _self:
+    SCRIPT_HASH = hashlib.md5(_self.read()).hexdigest()

+
+# Whether the Navi (gfx11/gfx12) kernel set is instantiated is a compile
+# definition decided by CMake (`VLLM_ROCM_ATTN_NO_NAVI`, see CMakeLists.txt), so
+# the units written here are identical for every build directory and arch list.

+FILE_HEAD = """\
+// auto generated by generate_paged_attn.py
+// clang-format off
+"""
+
+TU_HEAD = (
+    FILE_HEAD
+    + """
+#include "attention_kernels.cuh"
+"""
+)
+
+TU_ENTRY = """
+ATTN_ENTRY(paged_attention_{name}_bs{block_size}) {{
+  CALL_CUSTOM_LAUNCHER_OUT({query_type}, {kv_type}, {kv_cache_enum},
+                           {block_size}, {head_size}, {mfma});
+}}
+"""
+
+ENTRIES_HEAD = (
+    FILE_HEAD
+    + """
+// Prototypes of the entry points defined in the generated
+// attention_paged_attn_*.cu translation units.
+"""
+)
+
+DISPATCH_HEAD = (
+    FILE_HEAD
+    + """
+  // Dispatch on kv_cache_dtype, query dtype, mfma_type, block size and head
+  // size, mirroring the template parameters of the generated entry points.
+"""
+)
+
+
+def entry_point(variant, block_size):
+    return f"paged_attention_{variant['name']}_bs{block_size}"
+
+
+def block_size_switch(variants, indent_level):
+    """Switch on block_size then head_size for one dispatch group.
+
+    `variants` is the list of variants sharing (kv_cache_dtype, query dtype,
+    mfma_type); they differ in head size only.
+    """
+    indent = " " * indent_level
+    inner = " " * (indent_level + 4)
+    lines = [f"{indent}switch (block_size) {{"]
+    for block_size in BLOCK_SIZES:
+        lines.append(f"{indent}  case {block_size}:")
+        lines.append(f"{inner}switch (head_size) {{")
+        for variant in variants:
+            lines.append(f"{inner}  case {variant['head_size']}:")
+            lines.append(f"{inner}    {entry_point(variant, block_size)}(ATTN_FWD);")
+            lines.append(f"{inner}    break;")
+        lines.append(f"{inner}  default:")

+        )
+        lines.append(f"{inner}    break;")
+        lines.append(f"{inner}}}")
+        lines.append(f"{indent}    break;")

+    lines.append(
+        f'{indent}    TORCH_CHECK(false, "Unsupported block size: ", block_size);'
+    )
+    lines.append(f"{indent}    break;")
+    lines.append(f"{indent}}}")

+def group_variants():

+    groups = {}

+            variant["kv_cache_dtype"],
+            variant["query_scalar_type"],

+    kv_cache_dtypes = list(by_kv_cache_dtype)

+        predicate = KV_CACHE_DTYPE_PREDICATES[kv_cache_dtype]
+        lines.append(f"  {keyword} ({predicate}) {{")
+
+        by_query_dtype = by_kv_cache_dtype[kv_cache_dtype]
+        for dtype_index, (query_scalar_type, by_mfma) in enumerate(

+        ):
+            dtype_keyword = "if" if dtype_index == 0 else "else if"
+            lines.append(
+                f"    {dtype_keyword} (query.dtype() == "
+                f"at::ScalarType::{query_scalar_type}) {{"
+            )
+
+            mfma_types = list(by_mfma)
+            if len(mfma_types) == 1 and mfma_types[0] is None:
+                lines.extend(block_size_switch(by_mfma[None], 6))

+                # as the hand-written dispatch used to: any value other than the
+                # recognised ones keeps selecting that arm instead of failing.

+                        f"the {mfma_types} group needs an f16 arm, which is "
+                        "emitted as the catch-all else"
+                    )
+                ordered = sorted(mfma_types, key=lambda m: m == "f16")  # f16 last
+                for mfma_index, mfma_type in enumerate(ordered):
+                    if mfma_index == len(ordered) - 1:
+                        lines.append("      else {")
+                    else:
+                        mfma_keyword = "if" if mfma_index == 0 else "else if"
+                        lines.append(
+                            f'      {mfma_keyword} (mfma_type == "{mfma_type}") {{'
+                        )
+                    lines.extend(block_size_switch(by_mfma[mfma_type], 8))
+                    lines.append("      }")
+            lines.append("    }")
+
+        lines.append("    else {")
+        lines.append(
+            '      TORCH_CHECK(false, "Unsupported data type: ", query.dtype());'
+        )
+        lines.append("    }")
+        lines.append("  }")
+
+    lines.append("  else {")
+    lines.append(
+        '    TORCH_CHECK(false, "Unsupported KV cache dtype: ", kv_cache_dtype);'
+    )
+    lines.append("  }")
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+def generate_entries():
+    lines = [ENTRIES_HEAD.rstrip("\n")]
+    for variant in VARIANTS:
+        for block_size in BLOCK_SIZES:
+            lines.append(f"ATTN_ENTRY({entry_point(variant, block_size)});")
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+def generate_tu(variant, block_size):
+    return TU_HEAD + TU_ENTRY.format(block_size=block_size, **variant)
+
+
+def remove_old_files():
+    # Only remove files this script produced: a name match alone would delete a
+    # developer's scratch copy in the same directory.
+    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "attention_paged_attn_*.cu")):
+        with open(path) as fd:
+            if fd.readline() != FILE_HEAD.splitlines()[0] + "\n":
+                continue
+        os.remove(path)
+    for name in (
+        "attention_paged_attn_entries.inc",
+        "attention_paged_attn_dispatch.inc",
+    ):
+        path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, name)
+        if os.path.exists(path):
+            os.remove(path)
+
+
+def write(name, content):
+    with open(os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, name), "w") as fd:
+        fd.write(content)
+
+
+def check_dispatch_covers_entries(entries, dispatch):
+    # Cheap replacement for the configure-time guard that used to regex
+    # attention_dispatch.cu: every instantiated entry point must be named by the
+    # generated dispatch, otherwise its unit is compiled and linked for nothing.
+    for name in entries:
+        if f"{name}(" not in dispatch:
+            raise SystemExit(
+                f"{name} is instantiated but never dispatched: add it to "
+                "VARIANTS ordering/generate_dispatch(), or drop it."
+            )
+
+
+def main():
+    remove_old_files()
+    outputs = []
+    entries = []
+    for variant in VARIANTS:
+        for block_size in BLOCK_SIZES:
+            name = f"attention_paged_attn_{variant['name']}_bs{block_size}.cu"
+            write(name, generate_tu(variant, block_size))
+            outputs.append(name)
+            entries.append(entry_point(variant, block_size))
+    entries_inc = generate_entries()
+    dispatch_inc = generate_dispatch()
+    check_dispatch_covers_entries(entries, dispatch_inc)
+    for name, content in (
+        ("attention_paged_attn_entries.inc", entries_inc),
+        ("attention_paged_attn_dispatch.inc", dispatch_inc),
+    ):
+        write(name, content)
+        outputs.append(name)
+    # Record what is on disk next to the outputs: CMake checks this list instead
+    # of trusting a glob, and compares the key (script hash + arch list) so that
+    # a build directory with a different arch list cannot reuse these units.

detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

**Splits each paged attention translation unit on one more item: `block_size`.** `main` (#62475) splits the kernels per (query dtype, kv-cache dtype, head size), giving 12 units, and each of those units still instantiates *both* block sizes and picks one at runtime. **Thus, we now have 24 kernels instead of 12.**

We introduce a generator for these 24 units instead of hand-writting each file: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/generate_paged_attn.py

This PR is part of a 5-PRs series with #62717 (topk softplus-sqrt), #62718 (skinny GEMMs), #63364 (int4 skinny GEMM) and #63365 (fused MUSE-Spark op). All PRs are required for build time gain, see details below.

The single-arch rows are `pip install -e .` on MI350 (gfx950); the 9-arch row is the `setup.py bdist_wheel` described under *Validation*. All cold builds:

| build | `main` | this PR | All 5 PRs (#62921) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAX_JOBS=16`, gfx950 only | 107 s | 92 s | 87 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, gfx950 only | 85 s | 86 s | 50 s |
| `MAX_JOBS=64`, 9 archs | 1263 s | 1261 s | 472 s |

## Claims

- Splits each unit on one more item, `block_size`: the runtime `switch (block_size)` inside `paged_attention_*` becomes an entry point per block size (introduced as a kernel dimension by #8310, kept as a runtime branch by #62475), so 12 units become 24 and each instantiates half the kernels.
- 14 % off the single-arch build at `MAX_JOBS=16`; neutral at `MAX_JOBS=64`, where another unit is the tail.
- ~190 lines of hand-written duplication removed: 12 units, 12 prototypes and a 50-line configure-time regex guard collapse into one variant list, so an instantiation can no longer exist without a dispatch arm - which is what the guard used to check.
- Navi-less builds instantiate 11 % fewer device kernels per unit; Navi (gfx11/gfx12) builds are unaffected.
- Nothing about what runs changes: same kernels, same dispatch order, same numerics.

### Why five PRs

The two builds are bound by different things, so no single change moves both.

**Why the three single-arch PRs are all needed.** At 1 arch (`gfx950`, `MAX_JOBS=64`, `main` = 85 s) three groups take turns setting the wall, in this order:

1. topk softplus-sqrt (#62717) - 74.5 s, a single unit
2. paged attention (#62716) - 71.6 s, the slowest of 12 units
3. other skinny GEMMs (#62718) - 40.9 s, a single unit

#62717 takes (1) to 7.4 s, #62716 takes (2) to 31.1 s and #62718 stops (3) from becoming the next tail; with all three the tail moves to `selective_scan_fwd` (37.7 s) and the build goes from 85 s to 49 s. Drop any one of them and a ~70 s unit is back at the top, so the single-arch win needs all three.

**Why that is not enough at 9 archs.** A 9-arch build multiplies every unit's time by ~9, and the tail becomes two files that none of the first three touch: `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` at 1232 s and `csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` at 478 s. All three merged take the 9-arch build from 1263 s to only 1253 s. #63364 splits the first (its tail drops to 448 s) and #63365 the second (to 171 s), which is what reaches 472 s.

The `skinny_gemms_int4.cu` tail is invisible in a `gfx950` build because that file **only emits its kernels for RDNA (that is part of the 9-arch build)**:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L17-L19
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f4edf9f0f078ae67392510aafd1871288948a3c3/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu#L568-L579

`csrc/fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` fails differently: it has no arch guard, so a `gfx950` build compiles it for real - it is just 25 s there against 478 s across nine archs, which is why a single-arch profile ranks it as irrelevant (#63365).

|---|---|---|
| topk softplus-sqrt | 74.5 s | 7.4 s |
| paged attention | 71.6 s | 31.1 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | 40.9 s | 31.6 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 36.5 s | 37.7 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 25.0 s | 10.9 s |
| int4 skinny GEMM | 19.4 s | 17.5 s |
| **wall / average parallelism** | **76 s / 15.8x** | **39 s / 30.2x** |

| slowest unit per group, 9 archs (`MAX_JOBS=64`) | `main` | all 5 |
|---|---|---|
| int4 skinny GEMM | 1232 s | 448 s |
| MUSE-Spark | 478 s | 171 s |
| `selective_scan_fwd` | 288 s | 296 s |
| paged attention | 284 s | 286 s |
| other skinny GEMMs | not recorded | 247 s |

## Validation

### Single arch build

```bash
PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx950" VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=N \
  pip install --no-cache-dir -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation
```

MI350 (gfx950), four builds run one after the other in the same container, each from a cleared tree (`vllm/*.so` and `build/` removed first), so every number is a cold build with no ccache and no shared CMake cache. Run-to-run variance is a few seconds, so the single-PR rows are indicative:

| | MAX_JOBS=16 | MAX_JOBS=64 |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (`main`, `f4edf9f0f0`) | 107 s | 85 s |
| **this PR** (`089bbaf68a`) | **92 s (−14 %)** | **86 s (≈0 %)** |
| #62717 topk softplus-sqrt 114a66d0f5 | 107 s (≈0 %) | 85 s (≈0 %) |
| #62718 skinny GEMMs 78a62ceb1c | 110 s (+3 %) | 85 s (≈0 %) |
| #63364 int4 skinny GEMM 6271426e4f | 109 s (+2 %) | 87 s (+2 %) |
| #63365 fused MUSE-Spark 31de254fe4 | 108 s (+1 %) | 87 s (+2 %) |
| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | 87 s (−19 %) | 50 s (−41 %) |

Environment, one host: AMD EPYC 9575F (64 cores / 256 threads), 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (251 GiB each), ROCm 10.0, `torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx950`, `PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_ENABLED=0`.

| check | configuration | result |
|---|---|---|
| `paged_attention` vs a torch reference over the paged KV cache (GQA aware) | fp16, bf16 x head 64/128 x block size 16/32 x gqa 1/4/6 | max abs err 3e-4 (fp16), 5e-3 (bf16) |
| fresh configure with no generated files present | generator runs at configure time | configure + build + link OK |
| moved kernel/launcher code vs the parent commit | scripted `git diff` of the moved ranges | empty modulo the intended edits |

Repo tests for the kernels this PR touches:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py
```

`393 passed, 14 warnings in 1732.99s (0:28:52)`

### 9 archs build

The multi-arch wheel build with the 9 release archs of `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`, mold as the linker and sccache disabled, from a cleared tree (`vllm/*.so`, `build/` and `dist/` removed first):

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold" \
  PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151" \
  VLLM_DISABLE_SCCACHE=1 MAX_JOBS=64 \
  python3 setup.py bdist_wheel --dist-dir=dist
```

The 9 release archs, one build at a time, same container and same command:

| build | wall time | wheel |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (`f4edf9f0f0`) | 1263 s | 266 MB |
| **this PR** (`089bbaf68a`) | **1261 s** | **275 MB** |
| #62717 topk softplus-sqrt 114a66d0f5 | 1243 s | 269 MB |
| #62718 skinny GEMMs 78a62ceb1c | 1248 s | 266 MB |
| #63364 int4 skinny GEMM 6271426e4f | **600 s (−52 %)** | **257 MB** |
| #63365 fused MUSE-Spark 31de254fe4 | **1241 s (−2 %)** | **266 MB** |
| All 5 PRs (#62921) e9f5601585 | **472 s (−63 %)** | **270 MB** |

At 9 archs the build is translation-unit-latency bound, not link bound: every host link is sub-second, so the wall is one long unit at a time. The split does not move that wall by itself - what it changes is that the link keeps succeeding. Pre-reland `main` (`db3b0f0fae`, i.e. #62475 without `--offload-compress`) fails this exact build with `mold: error: ... relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against .eh_frame out of range`, the failure #62983 reverted for.

## Details

Device code generation for one instantiation set is ~95 s of AMDGPU backend time, so a single file holding every (dtype, kv-cache dtype, head size) combination made the wall clock of the whole build that file. #62475 split it by hand, which left three things to keep in sync: the files, the prototypes in `attention_dispatch.cu` and the dispatch arms (hence the `file(READ)` + regex guard). Generating all three from one `VARIANTS` list removes that coupling:

- one translation unit per (variant, block size) - `block_size` moves from a runtime switch inside the entry point into the entry point name, which is what lets a unit instantiate a single block size;
- `attention_paged_attn_entries.inc`, the `ATTN_ENTRY()` prototypes, included at file scope;
- `attention_paged_attn_dispatch.inc`, the kv-cache-dtype / query-dtype / mfma-type / block-size / head-size dispatch of `paged_attention()`, included in its body.

The generated units do not depend on the arch list: whether the Navi (gfx11/gfx12) kernel set is instantiated is a `VLLM_ROCM_ATTN_NO_NAVI` compile definition that CMake derives from `VLLM_GPU_ARCHES` and sets on the `_rocm_C` target, so every build directory and arch list uses the same files (two builds can no longer overwrite each other's units). What is on disk is recorded in a stamp next to the outputs (`csrc/rocm/.paged_attn_generated`: the script hash plus the exact list of files written, gitignored) rather than in the CMake cache, and CMake takes the source list from that list instead of a glob: a stray or scratch `attention_paged_attn_*.cu` in `csrc/rocm/` is no longer compiled into `_rocm_C`, and a partially deleted set (any `.cu` **or** `.inc`, not just "all of them") triggers regeneration. The script is also in `CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS`, so editing it re-runs configure instead of leaving stale units behind. Separately, `-ftime-trace` attributed 6.9 s of the 11.5 s host frontend of a unit to `<torch/all.h>`, which pulls autograd, nn and jit into code that only needs `at::Tensor`, the CUDA stream/guard helpers and `TORCH_CHECK`; the header now includes the ATen/c10 surface only, which cuts both the host and the device parse by ~2/3.

**Change in behaviour.** Only one, and it is narrow: a build whose arch list has no `gfx11`/`gfx12` code objects now raises `TORCH_CHECK(!is_navi, ...)` instead of running a Navi launcher that no code object backs. The `mfma_type` handling keeps the previous semantics (the last arm is a plain `else`, so an unrecognised value still selects the f16 MFMA kernels rather than failing). Numerics are unchanged.

**How the matrix got this big.** The instantiation space this PR splits was grown one axis at a time:

| PR | landed | what it added to the instantiation space |
|---|---|---|
| #8310 | 2024-09-13 | initial ROCm paged attention: 4 kernels over `{fp16, bf16}` x head `{64, 128}` x block `{16, 32}` x alibi `{on, off}` |
| #8577 | 2024-09-19 | fp8 KV cache: the `KV_DTYPE` / `cache_t` axis |
| #12348 | 2025-03-04 | partition/reduce rewrite: 4 -> 6 kernels (`mfma16`, `mfma4`, `reduce`) |
| #17139 | 2025-05-07 | fp8 output fusion: `OUTT` becomes `uint8_t` when `fp8_out_scale` is set = x2 |
| #17004 | 2025-05-21 | RDNA/Navi: the whole set duplicated for gfx11/gfx12, 6 -> 12 `__global__` |
| #22222 | 2025-09-15 | fp8 attention update: adds `MFMAType` (`Fp8` vs `F16`) = x2 on the fp8 path |
| #42755 | 2026-10-15 | `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` added to all 12 kernels = +50 % |

So the matrix this PR splits is a product of six axes. This PR adds none of them; it cuts the product into 24 units.

### Left to do

Follow-ups identified while doing this, deliberately out of scope:

- [ ] Split the units further along `alibi` / `fp8_out_scale`: measured a loss while each unit paid ~20 s just to parse `attention_kernels.cuh`, which is ~6 s now.
- [ ] Cheaper debug info for HIP kernels: dropping `-g` saves ~18 % of a unit's compile time at 1 arch and more at 9 (`RelWithDebInfo` applies `-g` to every unit).
- [ ] `csrc/mamba/selective_scan_fwd` is the next tail once the two per-unit splits are in (296 s at 9 archs, 37.7 s at 1): split or prune its instantiations.
- [ ] `<torch/all.h>` still comes in transitively via `rocm/dispatch_utils.h`, which ~50 TUs include; trimming it there needs a CUDA build check.
- [ ] `hipify_all` is a single serial command (1.9 s) that every compile waits on - worth parallelising once the wall clock is ~10 s.
- [ ] Not done here on purpose: folding the 12 `VARIANTS` dicts into a product of three tables and dropping the redundant `clang-format off/on` pair around the generated include - refactor churn that does not change the build outcome.
- [ ] Not done here on purpose: `MANIFEST.in` has `recursive-include csrc *`, so an sdist built from an already-configured tree would ship the generated units (harmless, they are regenerated; CI sdists come from a clean clone), and the ROCm build docs do not yet mention that changing `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` regenerates these units.
